passages.text: Then Job answered: “How long will you torment me and crush me with your words?
passages.sermon:
Job was a man who suffered greatly.
His friends spoke harshly to him.
Job answered them.
He said, “How long will you torment me?
How long will you crush me with your words?”
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ עַד־ אָ֭נָה תּוֹגְי֣וּן נַפְשִׁ֑י וּֽתְדַכְּאוּנַ֥נִי בְמִלִּֽים׃

passages.text: Ten times now you have reproached me; you shamelessly mistreat me.
passages.sermon:
Job spoke to his friends.
Job said, “You have reproached me ten times.
You have shamed me again and again.
You do not feel any shame.
You mistreat me without respect.”
passages.original: זֶ֤ה עֶ֣שֶׂר פְּ֭עָמִים תַּכְלִימ֑וּנִי לֹֽא־ תֵ֝בֹ֗שׁוּ תַּהְכְּרוּ־ לִֽי׃

passages.text: Even if I have truly gone astray, my error concerns me alone.
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
\r\nJob is a man who suffers greatly.
\r\nJob addresses his friends.
\r\nJob says, “Even if I have truly gone astray, my error is my own.
\r\nMy mistake affects only me.”
passages.original: וְאַף־ אָמְנָ֥ם שָׁגִ֑יתִי אִ֝תִּ֗י תָּלִ֥ין מְשׁוּגָתִֽי׃

passages.text: If indeed you would exalt yourselves above me and use my disgrace against me, then understand that it is God who has wronged me and drawn His net around me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
Job’s friends accuse him and look down on him.
Job’s friends use his disgrace against him.
Job tells his friends to understand something important.
God has wronged Job.
God has surrounded Job with His net.
passages.original: אִם־ אָ֭מְנָם עָלַ֣י תַּגְדִּ֑ילוּ וְתוֹכִ֥יחוּ עָ֝לַ֗י חֶרְפָּתִּֽי׃ דְּֽעוּ־ אֵ֭פוֹ כִּי־ אֱל֣וֹהַּ עִוְּתָ֑נִי וּ֝מְצוּד֗וֹ עָלַ֥י הִקִּֽיף׃

passages.text: Though I cry out, ‘Violence!’ I get no response; though I call for help, there is no justice.
passages.sermon:
Job is suffering greatly.
\r\nJob cries out, “Violence!”
\r\nNo one answers Job.
\r\nJob calls for help.
\r\nNo one brings justice to Job.
passages.original: הֵ֤ן אֶצְעַ֣ק חָ֭מָס וְלֹ֣א אֵעָנֶ֑ה אֲ֝שַׁוַּ֗ע וְאֵ֣ין מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: He has blocked my way so I cannot pass; He has veiled my paths with darkness.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about his suffering.
God has blocked my way.
I cannot pass through.
God has covered my paths with darkness.
I cannot see where to go.
passages.original: אָרְחִ֣י גָ֭דַר וְלֹ֣א אֶעֱב֑וֹר וְעַ֥ל נְ֝תִיבוֹתַ֗י חֹ֣שֶׁךְ יָשִֽׂים׃

passages.text: He has stripped me of my honor and removed the crown from my head.
passages.sermon: Job speaks in his suffering.\r\nGod has taken away my honor.\r\nGod has removed the crown from my head.
passages.original: כְּ֭בוֹדִי מֵעָלַ֣י הִפְשִׁ֑יט וַ֝יָּ֗סַר עֲטֶ֣רֶת רֹאשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: He tears me down on every side until I am gone; He uproots my hope like a tree.
passages.sermon:
God acts against me.
He destroys me from every side.
He leaves nothing of me.
He removes my hope completely.
He pulls up my hope like someone uproots a tree.
passages.original: יִתְּצֵ֣נִי סָ֭בִיב וָאֵלַ֑ךְ וַיַּסַּ֥ע כָּ֝עֵ֗ץ תִּקְוָתִֽי׃

passages.text: His anger burns against me, and He counts me among His enemies.
passages.sermon: God directs His anger at me.\r\nGod treats me as His enemy.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣חַר עָלַ֣י אַפּ֑וֹ וַיַּחְשְׁבֵ֖נִי ל֣וֹ כְצָרָֽיו׃

passages.text: His troops advance together; they construct a ramp against me and encamp around my tent.
passages.sermon:
God sends His troops against me.
These troops come together as one group.
They build a ramp to attack me.
They surround my tent.
They camp all around where I live.
passages.original: יַ֤חַד׀ יָ֘בֹ֤אוּ גְדוּדָ֗יו וַיָּסֹ֣לּוּ עָלַ֣י דַּרְכָּ֑ם וַיַּחֲנ֖וּ סָבִ֣יב לְאָהֳלִֽי׃

passages.text: He has removed my brothers from me; my acquaintances have abandoned me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
God has removed my brothers from me.
My brothers are now far from me.
My acquaintances have left me.
My acquaintances act like strangers to me.
passages.original: אַ֭חַי מֵעָלַ֣י הִרְחִ֑יק וְ֝יֹדְעַ֗י אַךְ־ זָ֥רוּ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: My kinsmen have failed me, and my friends have forgotten me.
passages.sermon: My kinsmen have failed me.\r\nMy friends have forgotten me.
passages.original: חָדְל֥וּ קְרוֹבָ֑י וּֽמְיֻדָּעַ֥י שְׁכֵחֽוּנִי׃

passages.text: My guests and maidservants count me as a stranger; I am a foreigner in their sight.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job suffers greatly.
Job feels alone.
The people in Job’s house see him as a stranger.
The guests in Job’s house treat him like an outsider.
The maidservants in Job’s house do not recognize him as one of their own.
Job is a foreigner in their eyes.
passages.original: גָּ֘רֵ֤י בֵיתִ֣י וְ֭אַמְהֹתַי לְזָ֣ר תַּחְשְׁבֻ֑נִי נָ֝כְרִ֗י הָיִ֥יתִי בְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: I call for my servant, but he does not answer, though I implore him with my own mouth.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is suffering.
Job calls for his servant.
The servant does not answer.
Job begs his servant with his own mouth.
The servant still does not respond.
passages.original: לְעַבְדִּ֣י קָ֭רָאתִי וְלֹ֣א יַעֲנֶ֑ה בְּמוֹ־ פִ֝֗י אֶתְחַנֶּן־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: My breath is repulsive to my wife, and I am loathsome to my own family.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
Job says his breath is repulsive to his wife.
Job says his own family finds him loathsome.
Job feels rejected by those closest to him.
passages.original: ר֭וּחִֽי זָ֣רָה לְאִשְׁתִּ֑י וְ֝חַנֹּתִ֗י לִבְנֵ֥י בִטְנִֽי׃

passages.text: Even little boys scorn me; when I appear, they deride me.
passages.sermon:
Little boys see me.
They scorn me.
I stand up.
They speak against me.
passages.original: גַּם־ עֲ֭וִילִים מָ֣אֲסוּ בִ֑י אָ֝ק֗וּמָה וַיְדַבְּרוּ־ בִֽי׃

passages.text: All my best friends despise me, and those I love have turned against me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a righteous man who suffers greatly.
All my closest friends hate me.
Everyone I love has turned against me.
passages.original: תִּֽ֭עֲבוּנִי כָּל־ מְתֵ֣י סוֹדִ֑י וְזֶֽה־ אָ֝הַ֗בְתִּי נֶהְפְּכוּ־ בִֽי׃

passages.text: My skin and flesh cling to my bones; I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
passages.sermon:
Job is the speaker.
\r\nJob suffers greatly.
\r\nHis body is weak.
\r\nHis skin sticks to his bones.
\r\nHis flesh clings to his bones.
\r\nHe barely survives.
\r\nHe escapes with only his life.
\r\nHe escapes by the skin of his teeth.
passages.original: בְּעוֹרִ֣י וּ֭בִבְשָׂרִי דָּבְקָ֣ה עַצְמִ֑י וָ֝אֶתְמַלְּטָ֗ה בְּע֣וֹר שִׁנָּֽי׃

passages.text: Have pity on me, my friends, have pity, for the hand of God has struck me.
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
\r\nJob is suffering.
\r\nJob’s friends are present.
\r\nJob says, “Have pity on me.”
\r\nJob repeats, “Have pity on me, my friends.”
\r\nJob explains, “God’s hand has struck me.”
passages.original: חָנֻּ֬נִי חָנֻּ֣נִי אַתֶּ֣ם רֵעָ֑י כִּ֥י יַד־ אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ נָ֣גְעָה בִּֽי׃

passages.text: Why do you persecute me as God does? Will you never get enough of my flesh?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
Job suffers greatly.
God has struck Job with suffering.
Job asks his friends a question.
Job says, "Why do you persecute me like God does?"
Job says, "Will you never be satisfied with my suffering?"
passages.original: לָ֭מָּה תִּרְדְּפֻ֣נִי כְמוֹ־ אֵ֑ל וּ֝מִבְּשָׂרִ֗י לֹ֣א תִשְׂבָּֽעוּ׃

passages.text: I wish that my words were recorded and inscribed in a book, by an iron stylus on lead, or chiseled in stone forever.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
He wishes his words would be written down.
He wants his words to be recorded in a book.
He desires his words to be inscribed with an iron pen on lead.
He longs for his words to be chiseled in stone forever.
passages.original: מִֽי־ יִתֵּ֣ן אֵ֭פוֹ וְיִכָּתְב֣וּן מִלָּ֑י מִֽי־ יִתֵּ֖ן בַּסֵּ֣פֶר וְיֻחָֽקוּ׃ בְּעֵט־ בַּרְזֶ֥ל וְעֹפָ֑רֶת לָ֝עַ֗ד בַּצּ֥וּר יֵחָצְבֽוּן׃

passages.text: But I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end He will stand upon the earth.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
Job knows God is his Redeemer.
Job says, “My Redeemer lives.”
Job believes his Redeemer is alive now.
Job says his Redeemer will stand on the earth at the end.
Job trusts his Redeemer will appear after all suffering is over.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֣י יָ֭דַעְתִּי גֹּ֣אֲלִי חָ֑י וְ֝אַחֲר֗וֹן עַל־ עָפָ֥ר יָקֽוּם׃

passages.text: Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God.
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
Job believes in God.
Job says his skin will be destroyed.
Job says his body will decay.
Job says he will still see God.
Job says he will see God in his flesh.
passages.original: וְאַחַ֣ר ע֭וֹרִֽי נִקְּפוּ־ זֹ֑את וּ֝מִבְּשָׂרִ֗י אֶֽחֱזֶ֥ה אֱלֽוֹהַּ׃

passages.text: I will see Him for myself; my eyes will behold Him, and not as a stranger. How my heart yearns within me!
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a man who suffers greatly but remains faithful to God.
Job says he will see God for himself.
Job says his own eyes will see God.
Job says he will not see God as a stranger.
Job says his heart deeply longs for this.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִ֨י׀ אֶֽחֱזֶה־ לִּ֗י וְעֵינַ֣י רָא֣וּ וְלֹא־ זָ֑ר כָּל֖וּ כִלְיֹתַ֣י בְּחֵקִֽי׃

passages.text: If you say, ‘Let us persecute him, since the root of the matter lies with him,’ then you should fear the sword yourselves, because wrath brings punishment by the sword, so that you may know there is a judgment.”
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
He warns them about judging him.
He says, “If you say, ‘Let us persecute him,’ you are wrong.
You think the root of the problem is in me.
You believe I am to blame.
But you should be afraid yourselves.
You should fear the sword.
God’s wrath brings punishment by the sword.
This happens because of sin.
God judges people for their actions.
You must know there is a judgment.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י תֹ֭אמְרוּ מַה־ נִּרְדָּף־ ל֑וֹ וְשֹׁ֥רֶשׁ דָּ֝בָ֗ר נִמְצָא־ בִֽי׃ גּ֤וּרוּ לָכֶ֨ם׀ מִפְּנֵי־ חֶ֗רֶב כִּֽי־ חֵ֭מָה עֲוֺנ֣וֹת חָ֑רֶב לְמַ֖עַן תֵּדְע֣וּן שַׁדִּין׃ס
